elements.element: The Agreement must be governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 states that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County must have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants jurisdiction to the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County must have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants jurisdiction to the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The jurisdiction of the specified New York County courts must be exclusive.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 expressly provides that the specified state and federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction. The temporary-injunctive-relief sentence is limited to “those courts” and therefore creates no outside-forum exception.

elements.element: The Agreement must be governed by Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any of the permitted fallback laws.

elements.element: If Delaware law is selected, the clause must designate Delaware courts.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Delaware law is not selected.

elements.element: If California law is selected, the clause must designate California courts.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because California law is not selected.

elements.element: If the laws of England and Wales are selected, the clause must designate the courts of London.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the laws of England and Wales are not selected.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position: New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts located in New York County. Removing the conflicting Singapore forum and limiting temporary injunctive relief to the same New York courts were necessary to make that jurisdiction genuinely exclusive. No unrelated commercial requirement was added, and the retained submission and waiver language is consistent with the selected forum. The fallback is not satisfied because none of its permitted governing laws is selected.
